P1.evidence: No setter pre-qualification existed to read back — the prospect's girlfriend made contact directly — so P1a drops out. The frame ran but at three parts, not four: 'I want to get a quick picture of where you're at right now. I just want to understand what's going on, what have you tried, and where you're trying to get to' plus a clean takeaway ('If not, no worries, we'll just shake hands and part as friends'); 'what's in the way' and 'what you need' were not framed. Agreement was requested and given — 'Sounds good?' 'Sounds good.' Open question ran verbatim in substance: 'walk me through briefly, what's the main thing you're looking to fix right now?'

P2.evidence: Strongest phase of the call. Work asked ('do you work right now or what does it look like?'), condition interrogated in real depth (radiation frequency, session count, remaining weeks, the four-week gap, twelve months of chemo, whether supplements were prescribed), injuries asked directly ('do you have, like, any injuries, or these are just, like, stiffness from all the...'), training week asked ('do you regularly work out with strength conditioning?'), diet asked ('what does it look like in terms of nutrition right now for you?') and probed for how long and how he was finding it, energy asked ('your overall energy levels, is that affecting in any way?'). Age, height and weight were never asked at all — a notable omission when programming for someone eight weeks post-brain-surgery. Results from current training never asked. Sleep was volunteered unprompted ('I'm sleeping a little bit more because of the radiation') and never asked, so it scores a miss.

P3.evidence: No aesthetics question and no 'something you want to do but can't'. The mobility/strength/energy question ran and was reflected back accurately: 'you basically want to get more mobility, gain strength, and get rid of the stiffness of the back and hips'. The bridge to deeper drive ran as a magic-wand variant: 'if you could have like a magic wand to solve this tomorrow... what would be the biggest relief... Or, like, what becomes possible afterward?' The 'who else does that impact' layer was volunteered by the prospect rather than asked — 'the main thing of being diagnosed with that is, like, people around you, the people that love you' — and the rep only echoed it back, so P3f is partial. The reflect-back was the best move on the call: 'So it's not only about like getting fit, like the most of guys that I talk to. It's actually about... getting you in a best position for a fight.'

P4.evidence: Not run at all. No question about what he had tried, what happened, why it did not stick, or what is actually in the way. The prospect volunteered the only relevant material unprompted — that he was 'a little bit lazy' before the diagnosis and would train once or twice a week, and that he wanted a home solution 'rather than plan for a gym, that I wouldn't be as motivated to do it'. The rep never asked why the gym motivation failed, which was the one root cause available.

P5.evidence: None of the four moves ran. The two-year question, the 'willing to settle' test, the 'why not' and the line in the sand were all absent. In fairness to the rep this is the one call in the batch where the scripted consequence frame would be grotesque — the prospect has already stated his own consequence, 'they would say, like, three to five years of life' — and the rep instead supplied reassurance. Recorded as a miss against the script, but the coaching point is that the script has no safe substitute here rather than that the rep should have run it.

P6.evidence: Belief check ran cleanly and in the right order, before any number: 'just to make sure that we are on the same page, if you have the right training, the simple nutrition, and Trevor in your corner, like, do you agree that you would actually get to your goal of feeling better and getting through this difficult time' — answered 'A hundred percent, yeah.' The all-in check was a weaker variant: 'if we can figure out the details, like, are sure you want to commit to this' rather than the scripted 'if you had everything you needed, is there any reason you wouldn't go all in'. A clear verbal yes was obtained before presenting — 'Let's do it, yeah, 100%'.

P11.evidence: A close was attempted, so the phase applies. Payment was not collected and the prospect explicitly asked for options in writing that were not sent on the call — 'if you can send me maybe a few options of how can we pay it or if there is payment plan'. Because payment never landed, the Trevor onboarding booking, the agreement email and signature, and the welcome-email and Skool walkthrough were all unreachable.

objection_plays.detail: 'I just need to check with my girlfriend' at 00:25:03. The opening move ran well — 'money aside, like, do you personally feel that this can get you [there]?' — and drew a strong answer. The rep also checked her alignment ('She's also, like, 100% on this?'). Everything else was skipped: no 'when you talk to her, what obstacles might come up', no 'is there any reason she would not want you stronger', no 'is this genuinely needing her input or asking permission to bet on yourself', no ownership frame, and no deposit-with-full-refund fallback. Instead the rep went off-script and asked him to wake her: 'Can you get her on a call right now? We can talk right now.'

Money was the only real blocker. The how-not-whether move ran almost verbatim: 'we're talking purely logistics, not like, should I do it, but actually how to do it in terms of finances?' The break-it-up move ran but was made conditional on the prospect naming a figure first: 'we can work around and maybe split it. But I would need to know from you what level of investments you can commit to at the beginning.' The permission question for an honest financial conversation was never asked. Of the six financial-picture questions only cash on hand was attempted, and vaguely — 'do you want to check, like, your checking account? Like, how much do you have?' — with no follow-up when the prospect deflected. Monthly surplus, credit cards, available credit, used versus available and investments were all skipped.

'we're going to think and I'm even going to make you an offer as soon as I speak to her' at 00:30:06. No OA move ran — no belief check on the plan, no 'thinking isn't the problem, deciding is', no 'what's actually coming up that's preventing you from getting started'. The rep moved directly to scheduling.

Script gap of the highest order. The prospect is eight weeks post-brain-surgery, mid-radiotherapy, seizure-onset, with twelve months of chemotherapy ahead and an unassessed back injury. There is no scripted move for establishing medical clearance or for deciding whether to sell at all, so nothing ran — the rep asked when the surgery was and how many radiation sessions remained, but never whether a clinician had cleared loaded ballistic training. The playbook's own known-gaps list covers a physio ruling movements out; it does not cover active oncology treatment, and it needs to.

Script gap — timing driven by a treatment calendar. The prospect wants roughly two months of preparation before chemotherapy and then faces a year of it; the programme sells 6 and 12 month terms with no way to talk about training through treatment. The rep did not address the mismatch and the prospect raised it himself: 'it's hard to commit for, like, big investments when you have something like I do.'

notes: Baseline and the commitment check were run properly and the reflect-back was genuinely good, so this is not a lazy call — but past attempts and root cause were skipped entirely and the money play was abandoned halfway. The overriding coaching point is not adherence: the rep needed a stop-and-check-with-a-clinician move here and the script does not give him one, so he sold instead. Second point: he asked the prospect to wake his sleeping partner to close, which is pressure, not urgency.
